correctness.rationale: A simplex cannot contain an antipodal pair, so the action is free and orbit labels order vertices compatibly with all face restrictions without conflating distinct orbit simplices. Adamaszek–Adams Theorem 1 gives simply connected covers with only free reduced H3, of ranks 9 and 49. Rational transfer and the halving of the Euler characteristic give ranks 5 and 25 in the quotient. Integral transfer kills torsion upstairs and its composite with projection is multiplication by two; the exact mod-two dimensions and UCT then leave exactly one Z/2 in H1. The cocycle taking the difference of lift bits records the transition between sheets, and the ordered simplex orbit model supports the Alexander–Whitney computation. An independently written replay at /workspace/branches/e245b7fb-638c-440f-b356-146d6918b70e/replay_orbit_cochains.py checks all signed d² identities, all orbit cells and the ranks (7,32,47,8) and (15,104,215,80,16). Its replay_output.txt records square rank increases 32→33 and 104→105, and cube increases 47→48 and 215→216, with both products cocycles. These dimensions and powers determine the displayed ring, not a space-level equivalence. The general line-bundle argument below separately proves the same groups and ring.

evidence: Write p:X→Y for the cover and x for its class. The rank-one mod-two Gysin segment is H^i(X)→H^i(Y) —cup x→ H^{i+1}(Y)→H^{i+1}(X). For i=0, p* on H^0 is an isomorphism by connectedness, so cup x is an isomorphism in that degree when H^1(X)=0. For i=1 the cup map is an isomorphism, and for i=2 it is injective. Hence H¹ and H² are generated by x and x² and x³≠0. For every i≥4 it is an isomorphism, so finite dimensionality forces all cohomology above degree three to vanish.

Rational transfer leaves only degree three in positive degrees and Euler characteristic gives its rank (c_n+1)/2. Integral transfer bounds the exponent by two, π1=C2 gives H1=C2, and the mod-two UCT in degrees 2 and 4 rules out 2-torsion in H2, H3 and all higher degrees. Thus mod-two degree three has rank (c_n+1)/2; all remaining products are fixed by degree. For c_n=9,49 this is the exact frozen result.

Nonzero x³ is forced by the low-degree exact sequence, rather than an extra geometric phenomenon of Q4 and Q5.

originality.rationale: The full asserted additive and multiplicative invariants, not only the fundamental group or nonvanishing cube, are routine consequences of the prior cover homotopy theorem and the classical rank-one mod-two Gysin sequence with transfer and UCT. No new special-dimension computation is needed to determine them. The later indexed four-cube homotopy-type result is materially overlapping, but the rejection rests on the prior implication, not on priority inferred from its date.
